verses.author: model_A
verses.text: My grandmother's hands remember a language I never learned.

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
flour on the counter
holds the shape of a palm
that pressed here before mine

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the kettle knows too—
that same click and sigh she'd wait for
before pouring anything

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
steam fogs the window
I write her name in it
before it forgets

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the recipe card
in her handwriting, worn soft—
I add water where the ink has faded

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
morning light finds the crack
in the mixing bowl
still holding its shape

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the flour settles
into the same low light
where her hands used to rest

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
a bird lands on the sill,
takes nothing—
just checking who's still here

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
steam fogs the window
I write my name in it
before it disappears

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the kettle clicks off
and no one calls out
to say the tea's ready

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
the calendar page
still turned to a month
no one has the heart to change

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
someone's shoes by the door
facing out now, not in—
easier to leave that way

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
a coat still hanging
holds the shape of shoulders
no one has come to fill

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
dust settles on the piano
where the fingers used to be
soft as a held breath

verses.author: model_A
verses.text:
window left open
a moth keeps finding its way
back toward the dark

verses.author: model_B
verses.text:
the porch light burns on
for someone who has the key
but not the reason to use it
